## History
### Early history
Sound of Music operated nine stores throughout Minnesota by 1978.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneyears-18) In 1981, the Roseville location, at the time the largest and most profitable Sound of Music store, was hit by a tornado.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14) The store's roof was sheared off and showroom destroyed, but the storeroom was left intact.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) In response, Schulze decided to have a "Tornado Sale" of damaged and excess stock in the damaged store's parking lot.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14) He poured the remainder of his marketing budget into advertising the sale, promising "best buys" on everything.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) Sound of Music made more money during the four-day sale than it did in a typical month.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneone-15)
Best Buy Co. logo from 1984 until 1986 (but the "Superstores" variant, added in March 1986)
Best Buy Superstores logo from 1986 until 1989

## History
### Early history
In 1983, with seven stores and $10 million in annual sales, Sound of Music was renamed Best Buy Company, Inc.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneyears-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) The company also expanded its product offerings to include home appliances and VCRs, in an attempt to expand beyond its then-core customer base of 15- to 18-year-old males. Later that year, Best Buy opened its first superstore in Burnsville, Minnesota.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) The Burnsville location featured a high-volume, low-price business model, which was borrowed partially from Schulze's successful Tornado Sale in 1981.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) In its first year, the Burnsville store out-performed all other Best Buy stores combined.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneone-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discount-16)
Best Buy was taken public in 1985, and two years later it debuted on the New York Stock Exchange.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-chainstore-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21) In 1988, Best Buy was in a price and location war with Detroit-based appliance chain Highland Superstores, and Schulze attempted to sell the company to Circuit City for US$30 million. Circuit City rejected the offer, claiming they could open a store in Minneapolis and "blow them away."[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-22)

## History
### Early history
In 1988, the company introduced a new store concept dubbed "Concept II".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discount-16)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-chainstore-20) Concept II replaced dimly lit industrial-style stores with brighter and more fashionably fixtured stores.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discount-16) Stores also began placing all stock on the sales floor rather than in a stock room, had fewer salespersons and provided more self-help product information for its customers.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-chainstore-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21) Best Buy also did away with commissioned salespeople.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-chainstore-20) The commission-free sales environment "created a more relaxed shopping environment free of the high-pressure sales tactics used in other stores," but was unpopular with salespersons and suppliers.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-chainstore-20) Upset that their products would no longer be pushed by salespeople, some suppliers such as Maytag, Whirlpool, and Sony stopped selling in Best Buy stores altogether.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneone-15) The suppliers returned after Best Buy's sales and revenue grew following the roll-out of Concept II.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19)
In 1992, the company achieved $1 billion in annual revenues.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21) Its Midwest rival, Highland, would file for bankruptcy in the same year and close all locations by 1993.

## History
### Early history
In 1994, Best Buy debuted "Concept III" stores in several new markets including Los Angeles and [Washington, D.C.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discountstorenews11-23) Concept III stores were larger than previous stores and included expanded product offerings, "Answer Center" touchscreen kiosks that displayed product information for both customers and employees, and demonstration areas for products such as surround sound stereo systems and video games.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discountstorenews11-23)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-customerelectronics-24)
Best Buy launched its "Concept IV" stores with its expansion into New England in 1998.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-discountstorenews26-25) Concept IV stores included an open layout with products organized by category, cash registers located throughout the store, and slightly smaller stores than Concept III stores.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribunemoore-26) The stores also had large areas for demonstrating home theater systems and computer software.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-providencenew-27)
In 1999, Best Buy was added to [Standard & Poor's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standard_&_Poor's "Standard & Poor's")S&P 500.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-internationaldirectory-21)

**Best Buy** is a big store that sells electronics like TVs, computers, and phones. It also sells home appliances. The company started in 1966 in St. Paul, Minnesota, USA. It was first called Sound of Music and focused on audio equipment.

In 1983, the company changed its name to Best Buy. It started selling more types of electronics. Best Buy has stores in the United States and Canada. It used to have stores in China and Mexico too. Best Buy also owns other companies like Geek Squad, which helps fix computers.
Best Buy is one of the largest electronics stores in the United States. It is a very important company in the retail world.

## How Best Buy Started
### The Sound of Music Years
Sound of Music logo used from 1980 until 1984
Best Buy began on August 22, 1966. A person named Richard M. Schulze opened an electronics store. It was called Sound of Music. This store sold fancy stereo systems. Schulze used his own money to open the first store.
By 1969, there were three Sound of Music stores. The company grew and made good money. By 1978, there were nine stores in Minnesota.

## How Best Buy Started
### The "Tornado Sale" Idea
In 1981, a tornado hit one of the biggest Sound of Music stores. The roof was torn off, but many products were safe. Schulze decided to have a "Tornado Sale" in the parking lot. He advertised it by promising "best buys" on everything.
This sale was a huge success! The company made more money in four days than in a whole month. This event gave Schulze an idea for a new way to sell things.

## How Best Buy Started
### Becoming Best Buy
Best Buy Co. logo from 1984 until 1986
Best Buy Superstores logo from 1986 until 1989
In 1983, Sound of Music changed its name to Best Buy Company, Inc. There were seven stores at this time. The company started selling home appliances and VCRs. This helped them reach more customers.
Best Buy opened its first "superstore" in Burnsville, Minnesota. This store used the idea from the "Tornado Sale." It sold many items at low prices. This new store was very successful.
In 1985, Best Buy became a public company. This meant people could buy shares of the company. Two years later, its shares were listed on the New York Stock Exchange.

## How Best Buy Started
### New Store Ideas
In 1988, Best Buy tried a new store design called "Concept II." Stores became brighter and more modern. All products were placed on the sales floor. There were fewer salespeople, and customers could find information themselves.
Best Buy also stopped paying salespeople based on how much they sold. This made shopping more relaxed. At first, some companies like Sony stopped selling their products at Best Buy. But when Best Buy's sales grew, they came back.
By 1992, Best Buy was making $1 billion in sales each year. In 1994, they launched "Concept III" stores. These stores were bigger and had more products. They also had "Answer Center" touchscreens for product info.
In 1998, "Concept IV" stores opened. These had an open layout and products organized by type. Cash registers were placed around the store. Best Buy was added to the S&P 500 list in 1999.

## Best Buy in the 2000s
Best Buy logo from 1989 until 2018
Former Best Buy Store in Shanghai, China
In 2000, Best Buy bought Magnolia Hi-Fi, a store that sold audio and video equipment. In 2001, Best Buy bought Musicland Stores Corporation. This company owned stores like Sam Goody.
Later in 2001, Best Buy bought Future Shop Ltd. in Canada. This was Best Buy's first step into other countries. Future Shop continued to operate on its own.
In 2002, Brad Anderson became the new CEO of Best Buy. He had worked at the company since 1973. Best Buy also bought Geek Squad, a company that fixes computers.
By 2003, Best Buy had over 600 stores in the U.S. They also started a "Reward Zone" program for loyal customers. In 2005, Best Buy stopped using mail-in rebates. Instead, they gave instant discounts.
In 2006, Best Buy bought a big part of Jiangsu Five Star Appliance in China. In 2007, the first Best Buy store opened in Shanghai, China. Best Buy also started selling only digital TVs.
In 2008, Best Buy started selling musical instruments. They also became the first store to sell Apple's iPhone. In December, Best Buy opened its first store in Mexico.
In 2009, Best Buy Mobile stores opened. These stores focused only on mobile phones. Brian J. Dunn became the new CEO of Best Buy. Best Buy also partnered with CinemaNow for online movie streaming.

**63**events on this timeline
1.   On August 22, 1966, Richard M. Schulze and a business partner opened Sound of Music, an electronics store specializing in high fidelity stereos in St. Paul, Minnesota.   
2.   In 1967, Sound of Music acquired Kencraft Hi-Fi Company and Bergo Company.   
3.   In 1969, Sound of Music had three stores and Schulze bought out his business partner.   
4.   Sound of Music operated nine stores throughout Minnesota by 1978.   
5.   The company also expanded its product offerings to include home appliances and VCRs, in an attempt to expand beyond its then-core customer base of 15- to 18-year-old males. Later that year, Best Buy opened its first superstore in Burnsville, Minnesota. The Burnsville location featured a high-volume, low-price business model, which was borrowed partially from Schulze's successful Tornado Sale in 1981.   
6.   In 1983, with seven stores and $10 million in annual sales, Sound of Music was renamed Best Buy Company, Inc.   
7.   Best Buy was taken public in 1985, and two years later it debuted on the New York Stock Exchange.   
8.   In 1988, Best Buy was in a price war with a Detroit-based appliance chain and Schulze attempted to sell the company to Circuit City for US$30 million. Circuit City rejected the offer, claiming they could open a store in Minneapolis and "blow them away."   
9.   In 1989, the company introduced a new store concept dubbed "Concept II".   
10.   In 1992, the company achieved $1 billion in annual revenues.   
11.   In 1994, Best Buy debuted "Concept III" stores in several new markets including Los Angeles and Washington, DC. Concept III stores were larger than previous stores and included expanded product offerings, "Answer Center" touchscreen kiosks that displayed product information for both customers and employees, and demonstration areas for products such as surround sound stereo systems and video games.   

12.   Best Buy launched its "Concept IV" stores with its expansion into New England in 1998. Concept IV stores included an open layout with products organized by category, cash registers located throughout the store, and slightly smaller stores than Concept III stores. The stores also had large areas for demonstrating home theater systems and computer software.   
13.   In 1999, Best Buy was added to Standard & Poor's S&P 500.   
14.   In 2000, two Florida consumers brought a lawsuit against the company, alleging that it engaged in fraudulent business practices related to the sale of extended warranties (or, more accurately, service plans).   
15.   In 2000, Best Buy formed Redline Entertainment, an independent music label, and action-sports video distributor.   
16.   The company acquired Magnolia Hi-Fi, Inc., an audio-video retailer located in California, Washington, and Oregon, in December 2000.   
17.   In January 2001, Best Buy acquired Musicland Stores Corporation, a Minnetonka, Minnesota-based retailer that sold home-entertainment products under the Sam Goody, Suncoast Motion Picture Company, Media Play, and OnCue brands. Best Buy purchased the company for $425 million in cash and the assumption of $271 million of Musicland debt.   
18.   Later that year, Best Buy acquired the British Columbia, Canada-based electronics-chain Future Shop Ltd., marking its entrance to the international marketplace.   
19.   Brad Anderson succeeded Richard Schulze as Best Buy CEO in July 2002.   
20.   In September of that year, Best Buy opened the first Canadian Best Buy-branded store in Mississauga, Ontario.   
21.   In October, Best Buy acquired Minneapolis-based Geek Squad, then a 24-hour residential computer repair business with offices in Minneapolis, Chicago, Los Angeles, and San Francisco.   
22.   Best Buy stores in the U.S. surpassed the 600-store mark and the company opened its first global-sourcing office in Shanghai in 2003.   
23.   In June, Best Buy divested itself of Musicland in a deal with Sun Capital Partners under which Sun Capital received all of Musicland's stock and debt.   

24.   Best Buy launched its "Reward Zone" loyalty program in July following an 8-month test of the program in San Diego, California.   
25.   Also in 2003, Best Buy's corporate offices were consolidated into a single campus in Richfield, Minnesota.   
26.   In January 2004, Best Buy hired Virtucom Group to revamp Best Buy's website and handle all of the company's online content.   
27.   In May, the company launched its "customer-centricity" program, which segmented its stores according to customer profiles. The program also called for employees to focus on specific customer groups rather than product categories.   
28.   In October, Best Buy completed rolling out Geek Squad "precincts" in every American Best Buy store.   
29.   In April 2005, Best Buy began eliminating mail-in rebates in response to negative customer reactions against them, and instead started giving out instant rebates via notebook computers.   
30.   In May 2006, Best Buy acquired a majority interest in Chinese appliance retailer Jiangsu Five Star Appliance for $180 million. At the time of the deal, Jiangsu was the fourth-largest appliance chain in China with 193 stores across eight Chinese provinces.   
31.   In June, the company opened Geek Squad precincts at Office Depot in Orlando, Florida. The market test was later expanded to Denver.   
32.   In January 2007, the first Best Buy-branded store in China officially opened in Shanghai.   
33.   Best Buy also expanded its Geek Squad market tests in March, opening Geek Squad precincts in FedEx Kinkos stores located in Indianapolis and Charlotte, North Carolina.   
34.   In March 2007, Best Buy acquired Speakeasy, a Seattle-based broadband VOIP, data, and IT services provider. The acquisition was worth $80 million, and under terms of the deal, Speakeasy began operating as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Best Buy. The company's products also became part of Best Buy's For Business program.   

35.   Best Buy was one of several companies named in a 2007 report by Greenpeace for purchasing raw materials or manufactured products derived thereof from logging companies that in the opinion of Greenpeace, contribute to unethical deforestation of taiga in Canada. Since that time, however, the company launched what it calls Greener Together to increase the energy efficiency of its products, and reduce consumer waste through more recyclable packaging and proper disposal of certain electronic components such as rechargeable batteries and empty ink cartridges.   
36.   In October 2007, Best Buy became the first consumer-electronics retailer to exit the analog television market, carrying only digital products that became mandatory in June 2009 by the FCC.   
37.   In February 2008, Best Buy opened its first store in San Juan, Puerto Rico.   
38.   On April 26, 2008, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) fined the company $280,000 for not alerting customers that the analog televisions it sold would not receive over-the-air stations after the digital transition on June 12, 2009.   
39.   In May, the company agreed to buy 50% of the retail division of The Carphone Warehouse, a London, England-based mobile phone retailer.   
40.   In July 2008, Best Buy announced that it would start selling musical instruments and related gear in over 80 of its retail stores, making the company the second-largest musical-instrument distributor in the US.   
41.   Best Buy became the first third-party retail seller of Apple's iPhone in September.   
42.   In December, Best Buy opened its first store in Mexico.   
43.   In February 2009, Best Buy leveraged its partnership with The Carphone Warehouse to launch Best Buy Mobile, a Best Buy-branded mobile retailer. Best Buy Mobile standalone stores were opened in shopping malls and urban downtowns. These Best Buy Mobile outlets were also added in all Best Buy-branded stores.   
44.   In June 2009, Brian J. Dunn became Best Buy CEO. Dunn replaced Brad Anderson, who was retiring.

# Best Buy, Co. Inc. set to close Florence, Alabama Store
Submitted by the Bond & Botes Law Offices - Thursday, February 2, 2017
After serving the Shoals area for close to 15 ½ years, Best Buy has announced it will close its Florence, Alabama store located at 398 Cox Creek Parkway on February 25, 2017.
Best Buy, Co. Inc. is an American multinational consumer electronics corporation headquartered in Richfield, Minnesota. Best Buy, famous for its “Geek Squad”, was named “Company of the Year” by Forbes in 2004. It was founded by Richard M. Schulze and Gary Smoliak in 1966 as an audio specialty store with the original name “Sound of Music”. In 1983, Sound of Music was renamed Best Buy Company, Inc. and the company began to expand its product offering to include home appliances and VCRs, opening its first superstore in Burnsville, Minnesota. It debuted on the New York Stock Exchange in 1987 and achieved $1 billion in annual revenue in 1992. In 1999, Best Buy was added to the Standard & Poor’s S&P 500. In the early to mid 2000’s it continued to grow by acquired other companies including Musicland Stores Corp., Future Shop, Ltd., and a majority interest in Chinese appliance retailer Jiangsu Five Star Appliance. Best Buy’s U.S. stores grew in total to more than 600.
Flash forward several years to the 2010’s. With its U.S. store total topping 1000, profits began to decline as online shopping increased. As with many other retail businesses the online shopping industry began to erode revenues and profits.
The Florence, Alabama location is one of casualties of the decline. The Florence store opened in June 2001. My wife and I were married in May of 2001 and moved to the Shoals area in June of 2001 and so I have fond memories of that time.

# Best Buy, Co. Inc. set to close Florence, Alabama Store
The store has 60 full and part-time employees. Best Buy spokeswoman, Danielle Schumann said the company officials decided not to renew the store’s lease citing lease cost, overall strength of the retail market, and shopping patterns of customers as all playing roles in decision. She said “We do not take these decisions lightly,” and thanked employees for their dedication to Best Buy. Florence employees may apply for open positions at other Best Buy stores with the closest being Huntsville, Alabama. Workers who choose not to stay will receive a severance package from the company.

# Best Buy, Co. Inc. set to close Florence, Alabama Store
Submitted by the Bond & Botes Law Offices - Thursday, February 2, 2017
After serving the Shoals area for close to 15 ½ years, Best Buy has announced it will close its Florence, Alabama store located at 398 Cox Creek Parkway on February 25, 2017.
Best Buy, Co. Inc. is an American multinational consumer electronics corporation headquartered in Richfield, Minnesota. Best Buy, famous for its “Geek Squad”, was named “Company of the Year” by Forbes in 2004. It was founded by Richard M. Schulze and Gary Smoliak in 1966 as an audio specialty store with the original name “Sound of Music”. In 1983, Sound of Music was renamed Best Buy Company, Inc. and the company began to expand its product offering to include home appliances and VCRs, opening its first superstore in Burnsville, Minnesota. It debuted on the New York Stock Exchange in 1987 and achieved $1 billion in annual revenue in 1992. In 1999, Best Buy was added to the Standard & Poor’s S&P 500. In the early to mid 2000’s it continued to grow by acquired other companies including Musicland Stores Corp., Future Shop, Ltd., and a majority interest in Chinese appliance retailer Jiangsu Five Star Appliance. Best Buy’s U.S. stores grew in total to more than 600.
Flash forward several years to the 2010’s. With its U.S. store total topping 1000, profits began to decline as online shopping increased. As with many other retail businesses the online shopping industry began to erode revenues and profits.
The Florence, Alabama location is one of casualties of the decline. The Florence store opened in June 2001. My wife and I were married in May of 2001 and moved to the Shoals area in June of 2001 and so I have fond memories of that time.

Florence employees may apply for open positions at other Best Buy stores with the closest being Huntsville, Alabama. Workers who choose not to stay will receive a severance package from the company.

**63**events on this timeline
1.   On August 22, 1966, Richard M. Schulze and a business partner opened Sound of Music, an electronics store specializing in high fidelity stereos in St. Paul, Minnesota.   
2.   In 1967, Sound of Music acquired Kencraft Hi-Fi Company and Bergo Company.   
3.   In 1969, Sound of Music had three stores and Schulze bought out his business partner.   
4.   Sound of Music operated nine stores throughout Minnesota by 1978.   
5.   The company also expanded its product offerings to include home appliances and VCRs, in an attempt to expand beyond its then-core customer base of 15- to 18-year-old males. Later that year, Best Buy opened its first superstore in Burnsville, Minnesota. The Burnsville location featured a high-volume, low-price business model, which was borrowed partially from Schulze's successful Tornado Sale in 1981.   
6.   In 1983, with seven stores and $10 million in annual sales, Sound of Music was renamed Best Buy Company, Inc.   
7.   Best Buy was taken public in 1985, and two years later it debuted on the New York Stock Exchange.   
8.   In 1988, Best Buy was in a price war with a Detroit-based appliance chain and Schulze attempted to sell the company to Circuit City for US$30 million. Circuit City rejected the offer, claiming they could open a store in Minneapolis and "blow them away."   
9.   In 1989, the company introduced a new store concept dubbed "Concept II".   
10.   In 1992, the company achieved $1 billion in annual revenues.   
11.   In 1994, Best Buy debuted "Concept III" stores in several new markets including Los Angeles and Washington, DC. Concept III stores were larger than previous stores and included expanded product offerings, "Answer Center" touchscreen kiosks that displayed product information for both customers and employees, and demonstration areas for products such as surround sound stereo systems and video games.
texts.1:
12.   Best Buy launched its "Concept IV" stores with its expansion into New England in 1998. Concept IV stores included an open layout with products organized by category, cash registers located throughout the store, and slightly smaller stores than Concept III stores. The stores also had large areas for demonstrating home theater systems and computer software.   
13.   In 1999, Best Buy was added to Standard & Poor's S&P 500.   
14.   In 2000, two Florida consumers brought a lawsuit against the company, alleging that it engaged in fraudulent business practices related to the sale of extended warranties (or, more accurately, service plans).   
15.   In 2000, Best Buy formed Redline Entertainment, an independent music label, and action-sports video distributor.   
16.   The company acquired Magnolia Hi-Fi, Inc., an audio-video retailer located in California, Washington, and Oregon, in December 2000.   
17.   In January 2001, Best Buy acquired Musicland Stores Corporation, a Minnetonka, Minnesota-based retailer that sold home-entertainment products under the Sam Goody, Suncoast Motion Picture Company, Media Play, and OnCue brands. Best Buy purchased the company for $425 million in cash and the assumption of $271 million of Musicland debt.   
18.   Later that year, Best Buy acquired the British Columbia, Canada-based electronics-chain Future Shop Ltd., marking its entrance to the international marketplace.   
19.   Brad Anderson succeeded Richard Schulze as Best Buy CEO in July 2002.   
20.   In September of that year, Best Buy opened the first Canadian Best Buy-branded store in Mississauga, Ontario.   
21.   In October, Best Buy acquired Minneapolis-based Geek Squad, then a 24-hour residential computer repair business with offices in Minneapolis, Chicago, Los Angeles, and San Francisco.   
22.   Best Buy stores in the U.S. surpassed the 600-store mark and the company opened its first global-sourcing office in Shanghai in 2003.   
23.   In June, Best Buy divested itself of Musicland in a deal with Sun Capital Partners under which Sun Capital received all of Musicland's stock and debt.
texts.2:
24.   Best Buy launched its "Reward Zone" loyalty program in July following an 8-month test of the program in San Diego, California.   
25.   Also in 2003, Best Buy's corporate offices were consolidated into a single campus in Richfield, Minnesota.   
26.   In January 2004, Best Buy hired Virtucom Group to revamp Best Buy's website and handle all of the company's online content.   
27.   In May, the company launched its "customer-centricity" program, which segmented its stores according to customer profiles. The program also called for employees to focus on specific customer groups rather than product categories.   
28.   In October, Best Buy completed rolling out Geek Squad "precincts" in every American Best Buy store.   
29.   In April 2005, Best Buy began eliminating mail-in rebates in response to negative customer reactions against them, and instead started giving out instant rebates via notebook computers.   
30.   In May 2006, Best Buy acquired a majority interest in Chinese appliance retailer Jiangsu Five Star Appliance for $180 million. At the time of the deal, Jiangsu was the fourth-largest appliance chain in China with 193 stores across eight Chinese provinces.   
31.   In June, the company opened Geek Squad precincts at Office Depot in Orlando, Florida. The market test was later expanded to Denver.   
32.   In January 2007, the first Best Buy-branded store in China officially opened in Shanghai.   
33.   Best Buy also expanded its Geek Squad market tests in March, opening Geek Squad precincts in FedEx Kinkos stores located in Indianapolis and Charlotte, North Carolina.   
34.   In March 2007, Best Buy acquired Speakeasy, a Seattle-based broadband VOIP, data, and IT services provider. The acquisition was worth $80 million, and under terms of the deal, Speakeasy began operating as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Best Buy. The company's products also became part of Best Buy's For Business program.

35.   Best Buy was one of several companies named in a 2007 report by Greenpeace for purchasing raw materials or manufactured products derived thereof from logging companies that in the opinion of Greenpeace, contribute to unethical deforestation of taiga in Canada. Since that time, however, the company launched what it calls Greener Together to increase the energy efficiency of its products, and reduce consumer waste through more recyclable packaging and proper disposal of certain electronic components such as rechargeable batteries and empty ink cartridges.   
36.   In October 2007, Best Buy became the first consumer-electronics retailer to exit the analog television market, carrying only digital products that became mandatory in June 2009 by the FCC.   
37.   In February 2008, Best Buy opened its first store in San Juan, Puerto Rico.   
38.   On April 26, 2008, the U.S. Federal Communications Commission (FCC) fined the company $280,000 for not alerting customers that the analog televisions it sold would not receive over-the-air stations after the digital transition on June 12, 2009.   
39.   In May, the company agreed to buy 50% of the retail division of The Carphone Warehouse, a London, England-based mobile phone retailer.   
40.   In July 2008, Best Buy announced that it would start selling musical instruments and related gear in over 80 of its retail stores, making the company the second-largest musical-instrument distributor in the US.   
41.   Best Buy became the first third-party retail seller of Apple's iPhone in September.   
42.   In December, Best Buy opened its first store in Mexico.   
43.   In February 2009, Best Buy leveraged its partnership with The Carphone Warehouse to launch Best Buy Mobile, a Best Buy-branded mobile retailer. Best Buy Mobile standalone stores were opened in shopping malls and urban downtowns. These Best Buy Mobile outlets were also added in all Best Buy-branded stores.   
44.   In June 2009, Brian J. Dunn became Best Buy CEO. Dunn replaced Brad Anderson, who was retiring.

## History
### Early history
Sound of Music operated nine stores throughout Minnesota by 1978.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneyears-18) In 1981, the Roseville location, at the time the largest and most profitable Sound of Music store, was hit by a tornado.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14) The store's roof was sheared off and showroom destroyed, but the storeroom was left intact.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) In response, Schulze decided to have a "Tornado Sale" of damaged and excess stock in the damaged store's parking lot.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweek-14) He poured the remainder of his marketing budget into advertising the sale, promising "best buys" on everything.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-businessweekbg-19) Sound of Music made more money during the four-day sale than it did in a typical month.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Buy#cite_note-startribuneone-15)

## How Best Buy Started
### The Sound of Music Years
Sound of Music logo used from 1980 until 1984
Best Buy began on August 22, 1966. A person named Richard M. Schulze opened an electronics store. It was called Sound of Music. This store sold fancy stereo systems. Schulze used his own money to open the first store.
By 1969, there were three Sound of Music stores. The company grew and made good money. By 1978, there were nine stores in Minnesota.
texts.4:
## How Best Buy Started
### The "Tornado Sale" Idea
In 1981, a tornado hit one of the biggest Sound of Music stores. The roof was torn off, but many products were safe. Schulze decided to have a "Tornado Sale" in the parking lot. He advertised it by promising "best buys" on everything.
This sale was a huge success! The company made more money in four days than in a whole month. This event gave Schulze an idea for a new way to sell things.
texts.5:
## How Best Buy Started
### Becoming Best Buy
Best Buy Co. logo from 1984 until 1986
Best Buy Superstores logo from 1986 until 1989
In 1983, Sound of Music changed its name to Best Buy Company, Inc. There were seven stores at this time. The company started selling home appliances and VCRs. This helped them reach more customers.
Best Buy opened its first "superstore" in Burnsville, Minnesota. This store used the idea from the "Tornado Sale." It sold many items at low prices. This new store was very successful.
In 1985, Best Buy became a public company. This meant people could buy shares of the company. Two years later, its shares were listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
texts.6:
## How Best Buy Started
### New Store Ideas
In 1988, Best Buy tried a new store design called "Concept II." Stores became brighter and more modern. All products were placed on the sales floor. There were fewer salespeople, and customers could find information themselves.
Best Buy also stopped paying salespeople based on how much they sold. This made shopping more relaxed. At first, some companies like Sony stopped selling their products at Best Buy. But when Best Buy's sales grew, they came back.
By 1992, Best Buy was making $1 billion in sales each year. In 1994, they launched "Concept III" stores. These stores were bigger and had more products. They also had "Answer Center" touchscreens for product info.
In 1998, "Concept IV" stores opened. These had an open layout and products organized by type. Cash registers were placed around the store. Best Buy was added to the S&P 500 list in 1999.
texts.7:
## Best Buy in the 2000s
Best Buy logo from 1989 until 2018
Former Best Buy Store in Shanghai, China
In 2000, Best Buy bought Magnolia Hi-Fi, a store that sold audio and video equipment. In 2001, Best Buy bought Musicland Stores Corporation. This company owned stores like Sam Goody.
Later in 2001, Best Buy bought Future Shop Ltd. in Canada. This was Best Buy's first step into other countries. Future Shop continued to operate on its own.
In 2002, Brad Anderson became the new CEO of Best Buy. He had worked at the company since 1973. Best Buy also bought Geek Squad, a company that fixes computers.
By 2003, Best Buy had over 600 stores in the U.S. They also started a "Reward Zone" program for loyal customers. In 2005, Best Buy stopped using mail-in rebates. Instead, they gave instant discounts.
In 2006, Best Buy bought a big part of Jiangsu Five Star Appliance in China. In 2007, the first Best Buy store opened in Shanghai, China. Best Buy also started selling only digital TVs.
In 2008, Best Buy started selling musical instruments. They also became the first store to sell Apple's iPhone. In December, Best Buy opened its first store in Mexico.
In 2009, Best Buy Mobile stores opened. These stores focused only on mobile phones. Brian J. Dunn became the new CEO of Best Buy. Best Buy also partnered with CinemaNow for online movie streaming.
